writeup.1: Walker Golf Things are Australian, which is what makes the drop land oddly and also makes it interesting. Blooming Grounds went live on 21 August, and Walker describe it as an ode to spring, to the opening rounds of the season and the flora along the fairways. In Melbourne that is exactly right. In Austin it lands in the back half of an August sitting at a hundred degrees.
writeup.2: Read it as a forward buy rather than a right-now one. The seersucker shirt and the Featherlite polo work in Austin immediately, the fleece hood is a December purchase, and the rest sit somewhere in between.
writeup.3: The collection runs to six pieces, $50 to $120, in sizes S through XXXL. One of them matters more than the rest: the knit polo has an entire landscape knitted into the body.
writeup.4: The distinction is a real one. Most graphic golf shirts are a print sitting on top of a finished garment. Walker built the artwork into the structure of the fabric instead, as a jacquard, where the picture is made out of the yarn itself. It costs more and it takes longer, and it separates a shirt with a picture on it from a shirt that is the picture. The same scene appears on the tee, and there it is a print, and the two sitting side by side make the point better than any description does.
writeup.5: The rest of the collection is quieter and runs on two marks. The Hedge Script is chain-stitched, with a small golfer teeing off out of the W. The Kookaburra is an Australian kingfisher and Walker’s recurring mark that turns up on a sleeve, a cuff or the back of a cap.
